statement: NVIDIA is reported to have cut the mainline Rubin Ultra HBM specification to 192GB in an 8-high stack from 288GB in a 12-high stack, described as driven primarily by HBM supply constraints and data center power limits.
why: A vendor cutting memory content on its flagship part is a direct admission that HBM supply, not demand, is setting what it can ship, and it comes with an expectation of further HBM price increases.

impact.mechanism: Reducing HBM per accelerator is a response to memory scarcity and power limits; it signals the memory constraint is binding even as it lets more units ship per gigabyte of HBM.

evidence.excerpt: NVIDIA's adjustment of Rubin Ultra's specifications is primarily driven by HBM supply constraints and data center power limitations.

confidence.basis: Secondary aggregator republishing another outlet and citing SemiAnalysis; the companion write-up cites the same SemiAnalysis origin, so this is one story rather than independent corroboration. Not confirmed by NVIDIA.

dispersion: conflicting same-key reports: statement/trend changed (trend rising -> falling); sources: KuCoin News Flash, NVIDIA Investor Relations
